key_insight: Cluster-weighted loss can steer deep surrogate models toward hard-to-predict turbulence regimes, improving Reynolds-stress prediction in solar subgrid modeling.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical path to more accurate and generalizable turbulence closures for solar and other multiscale fluid simulations.
method: Train MLP and 3D CNN surrogates on high-resolution StellarBox quiet-Sun simulations.
Cluster training samples with K-Means or hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC).
Reweight the loss by cluster-specific prediction error to emphasize high-error regions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that cluster-weighted training significantly improved CNN performance, with 34% lower MSE and a higher R2 score across heights and depths in the solar atmosphere.
watch_item: Cluster-based weighting may be sensitive to how clusters are defined and could add tuning complexity or instability if error distributions shift.
paper_title: Cluster-Weighted Training of Deep Surrogate Models for Subgrid Turbulent Transport
